newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells off 40 percent of pharmaceutical firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells off 40 percent of pharmaceutical firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state has agreed to sell off 1.114 million shares in Memphis Pharmaceutical and Chemical Industries at 50 pounds a share after the privatisation offer was more than 42 times oversubscribed, an official at the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) said on Sunday.

The Egyptian state holding company National Pharmaceuticals had originally offered to sell 500,000 or 20 percent of the 2.5 million shares in Memphis but increased the amount in view of the strong demand, the general manager of CMA information department, Mahmoud el-Shanawani, told Reuters.
Individuals get 587,784 shares, or over 52 percent of the offer, he said. But each individual will get only four shares because the number of applicants was so great, Shanawani said.
Investment firms and mutual funds got 162,330 shares, 14.6 percent of the privatised block of shares.
The parent company originally allocated 125,000 shares for individuals, 125,000 for mutual funds and investment firms and 250,000 shares for Memphis employees.
The company has said shareholders will be eligible for a dividend of at least 5.80 pounds a share for the financial year 1995/96, which ended on June 30.
Memphis increased its net profits 10 percent to 19.75 million pounds in 1995/96 from 17.94 million a year ago. Sales rose 8.5 percent to 117.64 million pounds from 108.42 million.
